.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Lingering showers and a strong thunderstorm
through mid-evening, then dry overnight and Saturday.

A broad upper trough and associated cold front will slide to 
the southeast tonight. Scattered showers and perhaps a strong 
thunderstorm or two could linger through midnight, primarily 
along and southeast of I-95. Damaging winds and isolated 
instances of flooding will be the main threats. As of 230pm, 
radar shows scattered showers over southern Maryland and another
batch moving over Lake Anna areas of Spotsylvania and Louisa 
Counties of VA. Another heavy shower is noted over southwestern 
Nelson County. Additional showers and thunderstorms could 
develop over the central areas of the Chesapeake Bay and Tidal 
Potomac and eastern VA through midnight. Dry conditions are 
anticipated overnight and through Saturday night as weak high 
pressure builds in. Storm chances return Sunday afternoon as 
southerly winds return and weak surface troughing develops.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Hot and humid conditions next week with increasing 
thunderstorm chances by midweek.

Models are generally in good agreement that a strong mid-level ridge 
builds across the southern U.S. and into the Mid-Atlantic during the 
early to middle part of next week. Well above normal temperatures 
for late August can be expected as highs reach the lower to mid 90s. 
Hot and humid conditions are likely as heat indices reach the upper 
90s and possibly the lower 100s. 

A more notable mid-level disturbance will progress from the northern 
High Plains to the Northeast toward the middle of next week. The 
ridge will be suppressed as a result, but it remains uncertain how 
much and how quickly this happens. The latest trend in the ensemble 
guidance is for the upper ridge over the Mid-South to be a bit 
further west. If this pans out, our area in the Mid-Atlantic will be 
in a more favorable location along the periphery of the ridge to be 
impacted by passing MCSs. Eventually, by mid week it looks like the 
upper ridge retreats enough to allow the shortwave troughs to move 
over our area. Several of the AI models indicate increasing severe 
potential at some point Tuesday through Friday, which is certainly 
possible given the high instability that will be in place, along 
with substantial upper-level support from any strong disturbance. 
It's also possible a back door cold front tries to drop into the 
area by Wednesday or Thursday, leading to greater uncertainty in 
temperatures.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
While most of any severe thunderstorms develop southeast of 
I-95, there could be a stray thunderstorm near CHO, DCA, BWI and
MTN that could bring a brief reduction in visibility and ceiling.
As convection wanes overnight, dry conditions are expected.

VFR conditions expected this weekend into early next week. Northerly 
winds shifting east Saturday, then southerly Sunday, but remaining 
around 10 knots.

&&

.MARINE...
A few severe thunderstorms could evolve over the Potomac and 
Chesapeake Bay through the evening, which may require SMWs.

Favorable marine conditions expected this weekend into early next 
week, with winds around 10 knots. North winds to start the day 
Saturday become east by the afternoon, then south on Sunday.
